scope: Complete exact-GLB rendered evidence against the original generated source board, including whole envelope, visible contacts, openings, occupied interior, circulation appearance, cameras and phone comparison. Asset acceptance for a local runtime trial only.
source_provenance: Original generated four-panel design board, not photographs of a real church. Front, oblique, high-oblique roof and interior panels are enrolled. Dimensions and hidden annex details remain conceptual interpretations.

resolved_previous_findings.closure: Facade-close and architecture-close views now show a continuous sloped timber perimeter bounding the glazed gable and receiving the vertical mullion ends. The former clear unfinished strip is closed.
Program and vault-interior views show extended pendant suspensions reaching the roof lining rather than ending below it. Lamp height and circulation remain unchanged.

holistic_findings: The gabled sanctuary, recessed glazed frontage, repeated timber frames, narrow side openings, rear slit and low rear-right annex remain a coherent complete building in all whole-envelope views.
Roof and wall contacts, aperture depth, glazing continuity and annex closure remain intact. The stray downpipe is removed from the annex interior.

Pews, altar and pendants establish the sanctuary program; tables and chairs occupy the annex. Clear central, side and cross routes are visible. Door leaves remain clear of the open entrance, and the shallow approach meets the indoor floor.

Neutral full-resolution views include complete whole-building silhouettes with margins. All sixteen renders and the phone board were inspected directly, rather than accepting metadata as visual proof.
The phone board clearly separates generated design reference from actual delivered clay exterior and interior. No textured or surveyed fidelity is claimed.
limitations: Actual browser placement, collision, walking-network behavior, saved reload, terrain and landscape integration require separate runtime verification.
Architectural-clay material simplification remains intentional. Photoreal timber, fine joinery and construction-detail acceptance would require a separate textured-keeper review.
No seed publication, engineering, accessibility-code certification or broad student activation is authorized by this review.
